## Problem

`sst.h:503-507` declares:

```c
int min(int, int);
int max(int, int);
int getch(void);
```

`osx.c` defines all three — but cannot include `sst.h`, because `sst.h`
declares `void pause(int)` and `osx.c` needs POSIX `pause(void)` from
`<unistd.h>`. So the definitions are never checked against the
declarations: a signature change surfaces at link time or as undefined
behaviour.

This is the same defect class #10 fixed for `tui_active` and
`tui_getch`, left behind because it needed a different home. `tui.h` is
the wrong place for `min`/`max`.

## Why it matters

Small, but it is the last of its kind in the tree, and `osx.c` is the
one file that cannot see the header everything else uses.

## Suggested approach

`stdio_is_terminal()` shows the shape that works: declare it in a header
`osx.c` can include. Options worth weighing:

- A small `osx.h` holding what `osx.c` provides (`min`, `max`, `getch`,
  `randomize`), included by both `osx.c` and `sst.h`. Keeps one
  declaration each and leaves the `pause` collision alone.
- Rename the game's `pause` so `osx.c` can include `sst.h` outright.
  Larger, touches many call sites, but removes the constraint rather
  than working around it — see the comment at `osx.c:29`.

The first is the smaller change; the second is the one that makes the
awkwardness go away.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `osx.c`'s definitions of `min`, `max` and `getch` are checked
      against declarations at compile time.

#!/bin/sh
# Checks that AGENTS.md stays the single source of truth for project
# instructions, and that CLAUDE.md stays a pointer to it.
#
# Rules drift into CLAUDE.md easily and silently: Claude Code's `#`
# shortcut appends there, `/init` rewrites the file wholesale, and
# tools that target CLAUDE.md by name edit it directly. None of them
# know AGENTS.md exists. Without a check, the result is two sources of
# truth that slowly disagree.
#
# The AGENTS.md checks matter just as much: CLAUDE.md pulls it in with
# an `@AGENTS.md` import, and if that file is renamed, emptied, or
# deleted the import resolves to nothing -- no error, no warning, just
# an agent session with no rules at all.
#
# Usage: instructions.sh /path/to/repo/root

set -u

ROOT="${1:-.}"
while [ "${ROOT%/}" != "$ROOT" ] && [ "$ROOT" != "/" ]; do
	ROOT="${ROOT%/}"
done
CLAUDE="$ROOT/CLAUDE.md"
AGENTS="$ROOT/AGENTS.md"

# The pointer needs a title, a sentence or two, and the import. Kept
# tight on purpose: headroom here is room for a rule to hide by being
# folded into an existing line rather than added as a new one, which
# the line budget below cannot see. A very short phrase can still fit;
# that one is left to review.
MAXBYTES=220
# CLAUDE.md is meant to be frozen, so this is the exact number of
# non-blank lines it has today, not a generous budget: a rule slipped in
# as plain prose adds a line and nothing else would. Changing the
# pointer's wording means changing this number on purpose. The prose is
# wrapped at 72 columns to match the rest of the repo -- rewrapping it
# much narrower will need a third line and trip this.
MAXLINES=4

## Problem

#9 made the panels follow the terminal, but only at the next repaint —
which is the next prompt. A resize that arrives while the game is
blocked reading (a typed answer, or `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`) is
noticed and correctly *not* treated as a keystroke, but nothing is
redrawn until the player answers.

On tmux the pane is left blank in the meantime, which looks like a
hang. `main` before #9 behaved the same way, so this is not a
regression — it is the half of the problem that fix did not reach.

## Why it is left

Rebuilding the windows from inside the blocking read was tried and
made things worse rather than better. Every combination attempted —
`resize_term` plus `wresize`, plus `touchwin`, plus `clearok(curscr)`,
plus `endwin()`/`refresh()` — either left the message window empty or
blanked the whole screen. Under a `wgetch`/`wgetnstr` that has not
returned, curses is repainting a screen it is still reading from, and
the results were not reproducible enough to ship.

## Suggested approach

Worth deciding rather than picking blind:

- Handle `SIGWINCH` with a flag and do the rebuild at a point where no
  read is in flight, rather than reacting inside the read.
- Or replace `wgetnstr` with a hand-rolled line editor, which is what
  would let the prompt be reprinted and the partially-typed line
  restored after a rebuild. Bigger, but it also closes the Ctrl-D
  wrinkle noted in `tui_readline`.

Whichever, the test to add is in `tests/tui.sh`: resize during a
`help move` pause, then assert the prompt is still on screen and one
keystroke advances exactly one page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A resize during a prompt or a pause leaves a correctly drawn
      screen without waiting for the player.
- [ ] The pause still needs exactly one keystroke afterwards.
- [ ] What the player had typed is either preserved or clearly

	if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		timeout 60 "$@"
	else

# $1 fixture name, $2 the whole script fed to the game, $3 the
# directory to play in (defaults to one of its own).
#
# A directory each, because a journey that freezes writes a save file
# beside itself and the next one must not find it -- except for the
# pair that is meant to, which passes the same name twice.
play() {
	name="$1"
	dir="$work/${3:-$name}"
	got="$work/$name.txt"
	rc="$work/$name.rc"
	mkdir -p "$dir"
	( cd "$dir" && printf '%s' "$2" | run "$SST" 2>&1; echo $? > "$rc" ) |
		head -c "$MAXBYTES" > "$got"

	status=$(cat "$rc" 2>/dev/null || echo "no-status")
	bytes=$(wc -c < "$got" | tr -d ' ')

	# Checked whether recording or comparing. A recording is only
	# worth having of a game that played properly; a comparison that
	# matches byte for byte can still be a game that started exiting
	# non-zero.
	if [ "$status" != "0" ]; then
		fail "$name: exited with status $status, want 0"
		return
	fi
	if [ "$bytes" -ge "$MAXBYTES" ]; then
		fail "$name: produced at least $MAXBYTES bytes -- runaway output?"
		return
	fi
	if [ "$bytes" -lt "$MINBYTES" ]; then
		fail "$name: only $bytes bytes -- the journey did not really play"
		return
	fi
	if [ "$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "$got" | tail -1)" != \
	     "May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost upon your home planet." ]; then
		fail "$name: no farewell -- the journey did not reach the end"
		return
	fi
	if grep -q 'Transmission ends' "$got"; then
		fail "$name: the game ran out of input before the journey was over"
		return
	fi
	if grep -q 'DEBUG:' "$got"; then
		fail "$name: developer chatter would have been recorded as truth"
		return
	fi
	# A carriage return at the end of a line is a leak from a file the
	# game read, and recorded here it would be defended by the fixture
	# forever. The pager's own wipe ends a line too; drop that shape
	# first, exactly as journey.sh does.
	if sed "s/$CR *$CR\$//" "$got" | grep -q "$CR\$"; then
		fail "$name: a line ends with a carriage return"
		return
	fi

	if [ "$UPDATE" = "--update" ]; then
		cp "$got" "$golden/$name.txt"
		printf '  recorded %s (%s bytes)\n' "$name" "$bytes"
		return
	fi
	if [ ! -f "$golden/$name.txt" ]; then
		fail "$name: no recording -- run with --update to make one"
		return
	fi
	if ! cmp -s "$golden/$name.txt" "$got"; then
		fail "$name: the game no longer plays this journey the same way"
		# cmp as well as diff: a difference in trailing whitespace
		# gives two diff lines that look identical.

		printf '  --- first %d differing lines, recorded vs now ---\n' \

		diff "$golden/$name.txt" "$got" 2>&1 | head -n "$DIFFLINES" |
			cat -v | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
		printf '\n' >&2
	fi

## Problem

`finish.c:352` prints the Romulan surrender line of the score sheet
with a plural and a singular format string. The plural one is a space
short:

```c

```

The plural lands its number at column 46. Every other line of the
score sheet — including that line's own singular form — lands at 47:

Small, and only visible when more than one Romulan surrenders — which
means only on a won game, since `rules.c` scores surrendered Romulans

read is the one with a digit hanging a column out of line.

is a recording of what the game does. The comment above the `won`
journey in `tests/golden.sh` points here.

Add the missing space to the plural string, then re-record:


evidence for the commit.

# Everything else here compares a fixture with itself, which cannot

# $1 fixture name, then one or more lines it must contain.
covers() {
	name="$1"
	shift
	f="$golden/$name.txt"
	if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
		fail "$name: no recording to check for content"
		return
	fi
	for want in "$@"; do

## Findings

### should-fix — `tests/golden.sh:342-344`: the "two answers" comment states a rule the game does not have

> `# Two answers at the end, where the journeys above need three: this`
> `# game ends itself, so there is no `quit` to confirm -- only the score`
> `# and play-again questions.`

Both halves are wrong. `quit` never asks for confirmation — `sst.c:406-412` sets `alldone = 1` and breaks straight out — and the journeys above do not need three answers. I re-ran `reports`, `ending` and `docking` with the trailing `n` removed and all three produced output byte-identical to their committed fixtures; the third `n` is unconsumed slack, not a required answer.

Failure scenario: a maintainer adding a journey trusts the comment, hunts for a confirmation prompt that does not exist, and mis-sizes the trailing answers — or, worse, "fixes" the older journeys down to two and believes they have found a behaviour change.

The real reason two suffice is worth writing down instead, because it is genuinely non-obvious: the game asks exactly two questions at the end (`sst.c:501` and `sst.c:507`), and the two `getch()` pauses on this path consume nothing, because `readinput()` uses `fgets` (`sst.c:656`) which has already drained the pipe into stdio's buffer, so `getch()`'s raw `read(0, ...)` (`osx.c:55`) sees EOF and returns `'\0'`. I confirmed that by replacing the first `n` with `Xn`: the pause did not eat the `X`, `ja()` printed `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`, and the journey then ran out of input. Suggested fix: say the game asks two questions here and the pauses eat nothing, and drop the comparison with the other journeys (or note their third `n` is surplus).

The guard still works (which is the point), but the summary contradicts the disk. Merged. Issue #55 is closed — `3a93d93` on `main`, branch deleted, working tree clean.

**What landed**

A `won` journey in `tests/golden.sh` plus its fixture. The key insight was that the issue's framing was too pessimistic: it assumed a scripted win was implausible because the `tournament` battery never comes close. But that battery plays longer, harder games — a **short/novice game has only 2–4 Klingons** (`setup.c:547`), and seed `tournament 23` puts all three in one quadrant. The whole game is one move and one phaser burst.

That let me skip both approaches the issue proposed, and both turn out to be unworkable here:

- A **Debug-only "win now" command** wouldn't exist in the Release build, where `golden` also runs.
- A **committed frozen save** is worse than it looks — `freeze()` is a raw `fwrite` of the structs, and `struct foo2` gains `idebug` under `-DDEBUG`, so a save recorded in one build type can't load in the other. Worth knowing if that idea resurfaces.

So: no production code, no binary fixture, no debug path.

**The part that isn't just a recording.** A fixture defends whatever it was recorded from, so a journey that quietly stopped winning would be re-recorded losing and match itself forever. `covers()` asserts the six lines only a win prints, and sits *before* the `--update` early exit, so a careless re-record fails too. I tested it in both directions.

**Verification**: 10/10 in Debug and Release locally, 40 deterministic runs, clean under `dash`/`busybox sh`/`shellcheck`, and all four CI legs green — including both macOS legs, which was the real risk for a byte-exact fixture. The seven pre-existing fixtures are byte-identical to `main` (verified via `git hash-object`, since `--update` rewrites all of them).

**Two things the recording exposed**, both flagged by review:

- The score sheet's plural Romulan line sits one column left of every other line — the format string at `finish.c:352` is a space short. Real and player-visible, and only ever appears on a win, which is why nothing caught it before. Filed as **#62** (you chose that over fixing it inline) and cited in the comment; the fixture records it as-is, per the suite's own "recordings of what the game does, not proofs of what it should."
- `won.txt` is the only fixture containing a live ANSI screen-clear escape, from a supernova announcement. `cat` it and it wipes your scrollback — noted in the comment to read it with `cat -v`.

Review caught two comments I'd written that were confidently wrong (a claim that `quit` asks for confirmation, and an inverted account of how the seed relates to skill/length). I verified both against the code and fixtures before rewriting them.

Still open: **#58** (galaxy vs the manual, small) and **#46** (TUI resize repaint, the hard one), plus the new **#62**, which is a genuine good-first-issue — a one-character fix whose entire evidence is a one-line fixture diff.
